lessons.title: Covalent bonding

slides.title: Fullerenes: C60
slides.oldHtml:
Fullerenes (e.g. C60)

Hollow simple covalent molecules of carbon
  • C60 (buckminsterfullerene): hollow ball of 60 carbon atoms — a buckyball
  • Separate molecules held by weak intermolecular forces → soft, slide/roll easily, lower melting point than diamond
  • Does not conduct electricity — electrons cannot jump between separate C60 molecules
  • Huge surface area & hollow interior (plus nanotubes!)
  • Uses: lubricants, catalysts, targeted drug delivery

slides.title: Fullerenes: nanotubes & uses
slides.newHtml:
Fullerenes: nanotubes & uses

Hollow cages and tubes with a huge surface area
  • Carbon nanotubes: tiny hollow cylinders of carbon — very strong and light
  • Hollow interior can trap and carry other molecules inside
  • Uses: lubricants, catalysts (huge surface area), and targeted drug delivery
